My name is Roberto, and I have been a nurse in oncology for thirty years. When I started, things were very different. We used to write everything on paper, and the paperwork used to take about two hours every day. Patients used to come from very far away, and many of them used to stay in the city for months. Nowadays, a lot of them do their treatment at a partner hospital near their home. The equipment is different too. The machines used to be huge and very slow. Now they are smaller and much faster. But one thing did not change. The patient still needs a person who listens. That part of my job is the same as thirty years ago.

When I was younger, I used to travel all the time. I used to visit three or four hospitals every month, in different countries. Honestly, I didn't use to have a home life. My suitcase was always open. Then the pandemic came, and everything changed. Nowadays, most of my meetings are video calls, and I travel only twice a year. Some people think video calls are worse, but I am not sure. I used to spend two days on a trip for a one-hour meeting. Now I spend those two days with my clients' numbers, and my advice is better. I still love visiting hospitals, like this trip to Sao Paulo. But now a visit is rare, so it is special.
